o: Phone companion declares INTERNET and ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE permissions, Trumore package query, launcher activity, action activity, and action receiver.
Phone application configures dynamic and static launcher shortcuts for Lock, Unlock, Climate, Defrost, Trunk, and Refresh actions.
TelemetryParser parses vehicle JSON payload into high voltage battery SoC, remaining range, charge rate kW, 12V battery, tire PSI, locks, climate, and GPS coordinates.
VehicleTelemetry checks 12V battery threshold (critical below 60%) and evaluates individual tire pressure warning states.
SecureTokenStorage and ToggAuthManager securely encrypt and persist user auth tokens, refresh tokens, and session expiration timestamps.
TvaApiClient performs HTTPS network requests to Togg TVA cloud endpoints for telemetry retrieval, lock/unlock, climate start/stop, and locate horn/lights.
TrumoreBridge verifies com.togg.toggmobile package presence, launching direct intent integrations or Play Store fallback.
TelemetryDatabaseHelper caches vehicle telemetry records into local SQLite database for instant offline dashboard restoration.
WearSyncManager and PhoneWearListenerService exchange telemetry data between phone and watch over Wearable Data Layer path /togg_telemetry.
Wear OS watch application declares android.hardware.type.watch, fine/coarse location, vibration, wake lock, standalone metadata, and tile service provider.
MainActivity renders AMOLED dark UI with high voltage battery arc, remaining range, 12V status, 4-wheel tire pressures, vehicle lock switch, and climate toggle.
ToggActionActivity and ToggActionReceiver execute headless vehicle commands for Samsung Modes & Routines and togg://action URI intents.
ToggLoginActivity presents credential input and handles session login with ToggAuthManager.
Wear MainActivity renders circular AMOLED watch UI with battery SoC, range, 12V indicator, and live compass bearing toward vehicle GPS coordinates.
Wear MainActivity launches Google Maps walking navigation directly to vehicle park coordinates.
ToggTileService provides Wear OS Tile for quick-glance battery, range, and 12V status without opening the main watch app.
TelemetryParserTest executes JUnit tests asserting proper parsing of vehicle battery, range, tires, locks, and location data.
validate-kb.cjs asserts JSONL integrity, entity and file ID uniqueness, source file existence, and index route consistency.
DigitalKey and DigitalKeyManager parse Trumore digital key invitations, deep links, URLs, and SE- reference codes, storing authorized credentials in SharedPreferences.
WearSyncManager broadcasts digital keys to connected Galaxy Watch nodes over /togg_digital_key and handles /execute_key_action execution on phone.
Wear MainActivity renders active digital key card with remaining validity badge and quick lock/unlock actions.
DigitalKeyTest executes unit tests verifying Trumore URI parsing, reference code extraction, expiration checks, and JSON round-trip serialization.
MainActivity home tab omits the vehicle hero photo card and centers the two quick action buttons (door lock and trunk).
MainActivity renders specialized 4-wheel tire pressure card structured around a central '+' cross axis with front tires positioned above and rear tires below.
MainActivity renders customizable circular quick action buttons at the top of the home page with persistent user reordering.
TelemetryDatabaseHelper and SecureTokenStorage persist vehicle GPS coordinates, park address, trunk state, headlights, and drive mode to eliminate cold-boot demo fallback.
MainActivity renders embedded Google Maps interactive view and parking address directly inside the vehicle location home card.
MainActivity lets users select Eco, Comfort (Konfor), or Sport (Spor) from the drive mode card or driving value, updates telemetry, stores it in SQLite, and synchronizes it to the watch.

ToggActionActivity and ToggActionReceiver support drive_mode_eco, drive_mode_comfort, drive_mode_sport, and drive_mode_next by updating persisted telemetry; activity and receiver sync the updated telemetry to the watch.
MainActivity toggles ready-to-drive from the quick actions bar, digital key action, and Digital Key home card, checking canStartDrive when a key is registered.
VehicleTelemetry exposes isReadyToDrive and withReadyToDrive while retaining backwards-compatible constructors and copy helpers.
TelemetryDatabaseHelper persists ready-to-drive in is_ready_to_drive and migrates existing telemetry rows.
WearSyncManager includes ready-to-drive state in synchronized telemetry for connected watches.
ToggActionActivity and ToggActionReceiver handle emotor, emotor_start, emotor_stop, and ACTION_EMOTOR_TOGGLE commands with digital key drive authorization.
READY toggling is available from the standalone Home e-Motor card and does not require a registered digital key.
Home quick actions exclude e-Motor, support user selection from the vehicle action catalog, and persist order in SecureTokenStorage.
Digital Key pairing and watch transfer controls are in Settings; the Digital Key card is suppressed from the Home grid.
SecureTokenStorage persists system, dark, or light app theme preference; MainActivity applies it on launch and after selection.
Home header shows model and update time without VIN; Settings shows VIN, and Home cards use Liquid Glass surfaces.

TvaApiClient uses FriendVehicleInfo only when an Owner ID is configured, appends it as ownerId, and otherwise reports descriptive primary vehicle 401/404 guidance; Settings persists the optional Owner ID.

MainActivity removes legacy SAM and refresh bottom buttons, formats header sync time from system published telemetry timestamp, and provides a resizable Liquid Glass home screen widget for Galaxy S25 Ultra displaying vehicle location, battery SoC, estimated range, and expandable tire pressures with 12V battery status.
ToggAppWidgetProvider renders the latest cached telemetry snapshot, or creates a demo snapshot from saved VIN and plate settings when the cache is empty.
The Android widget receiver is exported for launcher delivery; its provider metadata requests a 30-minute update period and uses the widget layout as its preview.
The widget expanded section uses FrameLayout as its divider so its layout is supported by RemoteViews.

TelemetryParser prioritizes vehicle hardware timestamps (including producedOn and sensor timestamps) over generic updatedOn, supports ISO and epoch formats, returns zero when no timestamp exists, and excludes the gateway response timestamp; the API client and dashboard persist only positive vehicle timestamps. MainActivity displays driving trip distances rounded to whole kilometers.

Home driving card prefers myTrip over currentTrip, falls back to odometer-based trip data, and displays rounded distance, formatted duration, average consumption, and average speed without emoji or badge headers; dashboard odometer remains an ungrouped integer, while the header shows vehicle synchronization and app refresh times separately, with app refresh persisted in SecureTokenStorage.

TelemetryParser treats odometerStatus readings and direct odometer values at or above 50000 as meters and converts them to kilometers; smaller direct odometer values remain kilometers. Vehicle timestamp selection checks data.timestamp then data.producedOn before telemetry sensor producedOn and updatedOn fallbacks.
Corrective fact for AF047: MainActivity source text is UTF-8 without BOM and the Home card label is YolculuÃ„Å¸um; this replaces the mojibake spelling recorded in AF047.
Corrective fact for AF048: vehicle sync selection reads data.timestamp, root.timestamp, data.dateFormat, then producedOn and other vehicle event keys; updatedOn is never used as vehicle sync time.
TelemetryParser accepts Turkish month names and dotted Turkish date formats in Europe/Istanbul time for vehicle sync timestamps.
Corrective fact for AF042: dashboard header shows full Turkish vehicle sync date and time independently from app HTTP refresh time, omitting refresh when unknown.
Dashboard lock, trunk, and e-Motor actions require BLE connection and persist or render updated state only after successful command feedback.
Corrective fact for AF034: headless lock, trunk, and e-Motor actions route through VehicleBleManager, preserve digital key start authorization, and only persist successful feedback.
VehicleTelemetry copy helpers retain the original vehicle sync timestamp when local command feedback changes state.
MainActivity formats positive vehicle sync timestamps with Turkish locale pattern d MMMM yyyy - HH:mm.

Trumore 2.1.25 SmartAccess BLE uses service f0002412-0451-4000-b000-000000000000, command write characteristic f0002413-0451-4000-b000-000000000000, feedback notify characteristic f0002415-0451-4000-b000-000000000000, and CCCD 00002902-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb.

Corrective fact for AF053: VehicleBleManager also scans for the SmartAccess service UUID or names containing togg, t10, or sda; GATT connection discovers services and enables feedback notifications before exposing CONNECTED.

Corrective fact for AF054: real GATT commands write A1 01 lock, A1 00 unlock, A2 01 trunk, A3 01 e-Motor start, or A3 00 e-Motor stop to the command characteristic; feedback notification resolves the pending callback, with a 2.5-second write-success timeout fallback that updates telemetry.

Home header lets users edit and persist the vehicle title in SecureTokenStorage, shows an enlarged centered plate badge, and stacks vehicle synchronization and app refresh timestamps on separate lines beside it.
Tire sub-card drawables use theme-aware card_inner/card_stroke and tire_low_bg/tire_low_stroke color resources, with light and night values, for legible theme-adaptive pressure boxes.

Widget map preview removes the live telemetry, map-link, and coordinate labels and their backgrounds; the top-right badge displays the full vehicle sync timestamp matching the app header, formatted as d MMMM yyyy - HH:mm in Turkish locale.

MainActivity propagates cached, rendered, refreshed, fallback, settings, lifecycle telemetry or vehicle-name changes to all home-screen widgets, and captures its embedded map WebView to the app-local widget_map_snapshot.png before refreshing widgets.

The widget selects active telemetry serialized as JSON in SharedPreferences before falling back to latest SQLite row and then a demo snapshot; its 12V bitmap uses the selected live telemetry value. MainActivity saves active telemetry when rendering dashboard state, after successful vehicle commands, and on successful API refresh; successful park-address geocoding also saves the address and location to preferences and telemetry to active storage and SQLite, then refreshes widgets. SQLite getLatest orders by insertion ID descending and inserts replace nonpositive timestamps with current time. Widget minResizeWidth is 180dp, preventing 1-column resizing; width thresholds 240dp and 310dp select 2-column charge+map, 3-column (+tires+address), and 4-column (+12V) layouts.

Home quick action row displays centered door lock and trunk buttons without its quick actions title; card customization is in Settings, and home customization offers battery, drive, tires, location, and 12V cards while suppressing controls and climate cards including from older preferences.

The widget map HUD removes live telemetry, map-link, and coordinate labels and displays the full vehicle sync timestamp matching the app header in its top-right badge; the range HUD continues to display its perspective road graphic, charging badge, and centered range text.

Expanded map preview overlays live GPS status, telemetry timestamp, a cyan beacon pin, and Google Maps label on a dark zoom-16 Carto tile cached in app cache; while a tile is unavailable it shows a coordinate radar and street fallback and fetches the tile asynchronously. Map tap opens turn-by-turn navigation when resolvable and geo view otherwise.

Corrective fact for AF069: the widget map has no Carto tile fetch or asynchronous tile cache; it displays the MainActivity local WebView snapshot when available, otherwise a local road-free radar grid, and map image taps launch Google Maps navigation with geo fallback.

Exported vehicle action activity and receiver require the app signature permission com.togg.companion.permission.CONTROL_VEHICLE; the browsable togg://action path is removed and vehicle commands from that URI are rejected.

SecureTokenStorage and DigitalKeyManager use AES-256 encrypted SharedPreferences backed by Android Keystore, migrate existing plaintext values into encrypted preferences and clear legacy stores only after commit, and fall back to private preferences if encryption is unavailable.
The app disables cleartext network traffic and trusts system certificates for togg.cloud, toggid.togg.cloud, tva-api.togg.cloud, and trumore.app; the Togg login WebView rejects third-party cookies.

Before BLE LOCK, UNLOCK, TRUNK, or EMOTOR commands, VehicleBleManager rejects expired or invalid saved digital keys and enforces canLock, canUnlock, canTrunk, and canStartDrive for the matching command.
Wear OS disables backup, stores the watch digital key in EncryptedSharedPreferences with migration from plaintext preferences, and listens for /togg_digital_key data changes.
PhoneWearListenerService accepts key actions only from connected sender nodes with exact allowed action strings and executes authorized BLE actions directly when MainActivity is absent.
When no digital key is saved, VehicleBleManager requires demo mode or a valid owner session token for BLE vehicle commands.
TelemetryDatabaseHelper keeps at most the newest 100 telemetry history rows after inserts and exposes clearHistory to wipe history.
Release builds enable R8 minification and resource shrinking with rules preserving telemetry and key models, widget and action components, and security crypto classes.
The phone dashboard presents trip distance, odometer, and separate vehicle update timestamps.

VehicleBleManager detects active Bluetooth connection via device reflection, supports broad vehicle name heuristics, scans for surrounding BLE devices, and maintains connection without disconnecting on custom GATT UUID absence.
AbrpJobService requests fresh telemetry through TvaApiClient and sends it through AbrpClient on a chained 7-minute one-shot JobScheduler schedule with a network constraint when configured.
AbrpClient sets consumption from lastTripAvgConsumption when positive, otherwise from positive currentTrip.avgConsumption.
AbrpJobService is non-exported and protected by BIND_JOB_SERVICE.
The ABRP open button launches com.iternio.abrpapp first, then com.iternio.abrp, then the ABRP website.
ABRP enablement, user token, selected capacity, and last successful transmission time are stored through SecureTokenStorage encrypted preferences.
AbrpClientTest checks required JSON telemetry fields, calculated state of energy, charging state, and optional coordinates.

The home dashboard always appends a full-width ABRP card after the configured home cards and location card; the card displays 7-minute sync status and vehicle telemetry and offers send, open, and settings actions.

The settings dialog content is vertically scrollable and includes an ABRP settings shortcut near the top; the shortcut opens a dedicated dialog for ABRP enablement, token, battery capacity, manual send, and app launch.

GezRouteBridge parses decimal coordinates from plain text, geo/query/map URL forms, and optional place names; it builds direct trumore-superapp:// and beta deep links, retains the HTTPS ShareLocation URL, and dispatches through targeted package, untargeted VIEW, then geo: fallbacks.
The ABRP home card offers a Gez route transfer dialog with clipboard prefill, manual paste, vehicle coordinates, and ACTION_SEND text handling.
GezRouteBridgeTest checks plain and Google Maps coordinate parsing and generated native, beta, HTTPS ShareLocation, and universal geo URI formats.

GezRouteBridge.resolve follows up to ten HTTP redirects, collects every valid coordinate stop in Google Maps directions paths in route order, resolves stop names with Geocoder, and designates the final stop as the destination; Navigation dispatch tries the targeted primary native scheme, targeted beta scheme, targeted HTTPS URL, alternate package native and HTTPS URLs, untargeted native and HTTPS VIEW intents, then a universal geo: intent.

The Gez transfer dialog resolves pasted or shared route text asynchronously, displays all multi-stop route stops with per-stop transfer selection, defaults to the final destination, and explains that vehicle navigation transfer uses Togg Trumore Secure Bridge.

GezRouteBridgeTest covers direct geo coordinates, extraction and order of all four coordinates in a multi-stop directions route, final destination selection, last !3d!4d coordinates, and native, beta, HTTPS ShareLocation, and universal geo URI construction.

GezRouteBridge resolves multi-stop routes from named or coordinate /maps/dir segments, origin/destination/pipe-separated waypoints, ordered !3d!4d and !1d!2d data coordinates, and non-empty lines; named stops are geocoded and all stops are retained in route order.

Trumore destination transfer uses targeted ACTION_VIEW ShareLocation and native deep links with package and universal geo fallbacks; for a multi-stop route it dispatches the final destination because the vehicle accepts one target. Multi-stop navigation opens the ordered directions URL, while single-stop navigation retains geo and navigation URI fallbacks.

Gez transfer dialog offers full multi-stop route transfer to Trumore and navigation, alongside individual stop transfer controls; route stops display numbered roles, names, coordinates, and selection state.

Unsolicited BLE feedback updates ready-to-drive, lock, or trunk telemetry through registered listeners; telemetry parsing derives ready-to-drive from vehicle and power status, explicit flags, or positive speed, and parses headlights state for dashboard rendering.

MainActivity routes supported geo:, google.navigation:, ABRP, and Google Maps VIEW data and non-key ACTION_SEND text or clip payloads to the Gez transfer dialog; singleTask launch mode delivers new intents through onNewIntent.

VehicleBleManager establishes TRANSPORT_LE GATT, reports CONNECTED only after locating the Smart Access command characteristic, rejects live commands without a ready GATT writer, and retains simulated command behavior only in demo mode.
MainActivity reports Smart Access GATT readiness separately from BLE service discovery and guides users with media-only Bluetooth pairing to scan for the Smart Access BLE beacon.
VehicleBleManagerTest verifies live command readiness requires a connected GATT writer and demo mode remains ready without physical GATT.

AbrpClient.fetchLatestPlan requests ABRP get_latest_plan and parsePlanJson extracts the upcoming stop name, coordinates, arrival state of charge, distance, and duration from stop or waypoint responses.
SecureTokenStorage encrypts the ABRP route-sync toggle, last dispatched stop key, last route-check time, and active stop name with the existing secure preferences.
TvaApiClient sends destination and VIN to Togg Cloud PlannedJourneys with Bearer authentication and retries once after refreshing an expired access token.

AbrpJobService keeps the existing 7-minute telemetry job and runs an independent 15-minute ABRP route job; changed upcoming-stop coordinates are sent to Togg Cloud, persisted, and reported by notification, with Trumore car-display fallback.

ABRP settings control 15-minute route tracking separately from 7-minute telemetry, and the dashboard card shows route-sync state and the active stop; the Gez dialog offers direct Togg Cloud dispatch with Trumore car-display fallback.
GezRouteBridge builds and opens the Trumore car-display directions deep link with destination coordinates and name.
AbrpClientTest parses upcoming-stop objects and waypoint arrays from latest-plan JSON, including coordinates and route metrics, and rejects stops without coordinates.
TvaApiClient.sendRouteToVehicle posts the final route destination and includes ordered stop coordinates and names in the PlannedJourneys payload when multiple stops are present.

The Gez dialog exposes prominent and dialog-action one-click Togg Cloud dispatch for the resolved route, plus a direct Cloud dispatch action on each stop card; Trumore and navigation actions remain available.

Corrective fact for AF006: TvaApiClient fetches telemetry and sends PlannedJourneys destinations; it has no climate-control API. Phone climate, temperature, defrost, and related shortcut/automation controls are disabled and report that the vehicle feature is unavailable.

Corrective fact for AF015: watch walking navigation first opens google.navigation with mode=w and falls back to a geo pin only if that intent cannot be opened; missing vehicle coordinates prevent navigation.

Phone digital-key lock, unlock, and trunk actions use VehicleBleManager and update persisted or rendered state only after successful command feedback; climate, headlights, and drive-mode controls do not fabricate vehicle state.

Corrective fact for AF009: a watch telemetry refresh request asks TvaApiClient for fresh telemetry, then falls back to phone activity or SQLite telemetry only when the live request is unavailable or fails.
With no watch telemetry cached, the watch app and Tile show unavailable values and do not present sample battery, tire, or vehicle-location data as synchronized telemetry.
Watch GPS location updates are requested while the activity is resumed, removed when it stops, and initialized again after location permission is granted.

Missing or invalid vehicle coordinates parse as 0,0; demo snapshots contain no vehicle location, and the phone dashboard, action shortcut, widget, and watch refuse to navigate to a fabricated fallback coordinate.
Corrective fact for AF107: AbrpJobService records a stop as dispatched only after Togg Cloud reports success; opening the Trumore fallback does not suppress retries for that stop.
Watch digital-key commands route through phone BLE handling whether or not MainActivity is open, and the phone sends the command result back to the watch; only successful feedback updates telemetry.
Phone UI, shortcut, and automation lock, unlock, and trunk actions enforce the active digital key's matching permission before sending a BLE command.

Corrective fact for AF059: the supplied Trumore 2.1.25 libapp.so contains the 2412, 2413, and 2415 UUID literals, but literal presence does not independently prove their service/write/feedback roles or command encoding; APK SHA-256 and byte offsets are recorded in the verification report.

Original Trumore native Smart Access methods generate user/VIN-bound AndroidKeyStore EC secp256r1 keypairs and sign data with SHA256withECDSA; its Flutter binary contains certificate, challenge, status-signature, and counter vocabulary. Companion has not implemented this provisioning/session protocol.

Corrective fact for AF061, AF096 BLE feedback handling, AF115, and AF121: VehicleBleManager now rejects unverified live vehicle commands without writing guessed A1/A2/A3 frames or inferring telemetry from write acknowledgments/notifications. Only explicit demo connections simulate vehicle state; phone/watch callers receive the failed live result.

Corrective fact for AF060: CONNECTED is exposed only after discovering required characteristics and a successful CCCD subscription callback; notify or indicate properties determine the subscription value. This proves GATT transport readiness only, not authenticated vehicle-command readiness.

Corrective fact for AF019 authorization: invitations, reference codes, and imported JSON create inactive metadata with no granted permissions; arbitrary text is rejected and missing tokens, expiry, or permissions are not fabricated. Local key validity honors validFrom and requires an explicit expiry; UI displays activation pending.

READY uses exact supported state strings or an explicit boolean, with explicit false taking precedence; NOT_READY, INACTIVE, IGNITION_OFF, ACCESSORY, historical average speed, and a prior true flag cannot make fresh false telemetry READY. Not charging alone does not imply READY on the watch.

Original Trumore widget Retrofit call chains confirm tva-api VehicleInfo/FriendVehicleInfo, vin/ownerId, Bearer auth, Trumore Home Widget User-Agent, x-app-version 661, and toggid refresh-token form fields matching Companion. Initial OAuth redirect/scopes remain unverified.

Original libapp.so contains PlannedJourneys and carDisplayDirections path strings; AF106, AF109, and AF111 describe Companion implementation only, not independently verified external JSON/query schema, multi-stop support, or physical vehicle delivery.

Telemetry requests use demo data only in explicit demo mode; non-demo invalid session, network/HTTP errors, and corrupt JSON return cached telemetry or null instead of demo snapshots. Vehicle permission errors are detected even without Owner ID. Missing either coordinate makes the location unknown while valid negative latitude remains usable.

Regression checks cover negative READY states, explicit false precedence, missing coordinates, malformed telemetry, inactive key invitations, and transport-ready but unverified live-command rejection; the 57-test JVM suite and both Android debug builds passed during APK verification, without a connected physical device.

Further original APK AOT analysis recovers serialized CarCommands values DOOR_CLOSE=0x01, DOOR_OPEN=0x02, ETG_OPEN=0x04, ETG_CLOSE=0x05, CAR_START=0x0e; encoder 0x19fa42c puts the command value followed by seven UTC date/time bytes into an eight-byte payload. e-Motor stop/accessory transition remains unverified.

Original AOT chain 0x2296c3c concatenates the car command payload with the received challenge, invokes native signMsg(data,truId,vin), appends the signature, and wraps APP_USER_CMD_MSG=0x23 before its send path. This independently contradicts the old bare A1/A2/A3 packets; Companion still lacks full provisioning/session/status integration.

Corrective fact for AF130 schema limitation: AOT builder Gec 0x1881a5c, POST 0x2256014, and serializer 0xf53ac4 independently confirm PlannedJourneyRequest startingPoint/arrivalPoint/waypoints with nested geoLocation numeric latitude/longitude and address.label; this POST has no VIN insertion in its query/body and does not prove physical vehicle delivery.

Missing non-demo invitation VIN/plate remain empty and phone/watch show unknown vehicle metadata; explicit demo sample metadata and provided real values are preserved. Nested target invitations are limited to four redirections and query values are not double URL-decoded.

Corrective fact for AF129 initial redirect limitation: original prod.env public clientId, redirectUrl, and tokenLink match Companion; AUTH_LINK runtime getter uses the /realms auth path while lowercase authLink contains /auth/realms. Both variants exist in the APK, so no initial-login path repair is justified from configuration alone; initial scope list remains missing.

Companion now builds the original nested PlannedJourneyRequest shape, treating explicit route first/last points as start/arrival and only intermediate points as waypoints. A single target may use valid cached coordinates only from the same VIN as its origin; unknown origins are omitted and invalid target coordinates are rejected.

PlannedJourneys HTTP 2xx feedback states that Togg Cloud accepted the route; it does not claim vehicle-screen delivery. Startup-without-origin acceptance, account/active-vehicle routing, and physical delivery still need runtime evidence.

Five PlannedJourneyRequest JSON regression tests cover nested points, unknown origins, ordered intermediate waypoints, two-stop routes, and invalid coordinates; the final suite totals 62 passing tests and both debug APK builds pass after the original APK comparison changes.

Phone route feedback and ABRP notifications display the API callback's Cloud-acceptance message instead of claiming transfer to the vehicle screen. Phone BLE handling no longer announces that an unimplemented live command is being sent before receiving its rejection.

Original AOT data frame encoder 0x1f0bf30 writes an eight-byte type/block/LE16 lengths/block-count header followed by payload; default total packet capacity 247 yields payload chunks of 239. Request encoder 0x1f0c23c writes type/state/LE16 Iuu/LE32 Juu; Iuu/Juu higher-level semantics and full interoperable session handling remain unresolved.

Original SAM_APP_STATUS handler 0x2294454 accepts a complete 85-byte payload only after checking a strictly increasing six-byte little-endian counter and a 64-byte signature over the first 21 bytes against the stored car public key; the fifteen-byte status bit mapping and correlated command completion still need recovery/integration.

Original certificate call sites build phonePublicKey, vin and signed shortCertificateBase64 data; GetCertificate response validation checks VIN and local-public-key consistency before caching. Complete certificate schemas and reflected HTTP verb/parameter-placement/authorization contracts remain unresolved, so Companion does not fabricate provisioning requests.

Corrective fact for AF124 and AF134 integration limitation: Companion now creates user/VIN-bound AndroidKeyStore P-256 keypairs, raw 64-byte SHA256withECDSA signatures, accepted server certificates and a reactive signed Smart Access session.

Original AOT access-token sub -> trumore_user_id -> certificate header data flow is recovered; Smart Access suggests and validates the authenticated UUID subject and never derives it from a shared SE invitation.

Version 1 full certificates have 247 bytes: version, 53-byte UUID/VIN/UTC validity/permission header, phone key65, owner signature64, issuer signature64; relative header permissions47/48/49 are door/trunk/drive. Signature bytes are not a SAM key.

Corrective fact for AF144: original factory/getter/wrapper chains prove TVA_HOST_URL + /smart-access/api/v1/Certificates, GET GetCertificate with hex phonePublicKey/vin/isOwner query, POST CreateCertificate with public-key query and vin/shortCertificateBase64/isOwnerCertificate JSON body, Bearer auth and x-app-build-number.

Owner creation signs a genuine version1 183-byte short certificate with the local private key using recovered production defaults; only fetched full server certificates grant runtime permissions. Pending post-create generation requires a later fetch and cannot enable commands.

Reactive authentication requires accepted certificate transfer, phone proof of SAM nonce, SAM proof of a new phone nonce and a fresh signed status before READY; first selected SAM key is encrypted and pinned per user/VIN, and changed keys are rejected.

Corrective fact for AF142: PRE ACK contains accumulated received payload length and next block number; COMPLETE contains total payload length and zero. Frames validate IDs/order/lengths/block count, use MTU-dependent capacity and serialized Android GATT writes.

Corrective fact for AF143: 85-byte SAM status has decoded named15-byte fields plus counter6LE and signature64 over first21 bytes; strict increasing counter and P-256 signature are required. Power ON3 is accessory and original READY consumers select Driving4.

Corrective fact for AF125 live rejection: authenticated live sessions now send recovered lock01/unlock02/trunkOpen04/trunkClose05/motorStart0e command envelopes. Unauthenticated sessions remain rejected; motor stop/accessory return is unverified and never synthesized.

Corrective fact for AF122: live phone/dashboard/shortcut/automation/watch commands use coordinator certificate permissions and verified session; legacy inactive invitation metadata neither grants permission nor blocks valid server-provisioned BLE access.

Successful command feedback requires command ACK followed by newer signed status matching its physical target; GATT ACK alone cannot succeed. Freshness/range/drive readiness and one-command-at-a-time guards apply; timeout or session validation failure closes BLE against late feedback.

Smart Access setup offers real VIN, automatic account UUID, fetch/create certificate, cached-key authentication and sanitized shareable diagnostics without raw tokens/keys/certificates/UUID/VIN/challenges/signatures; access states and last command result are visible.

Verified active server-certificate metadata enables the existing watch relay UI while private keys remain in phone AndroidKeyStore; watch connected-node requests are handled by phone BLE session and receive actual command results.

Fresh signed BLE status overlays lock/door/trunk/window/READY fields only; unrelated cloud telemetry and its timestamp are preserved so old battery/location data is not labeled freshly observed over BLE.

Certificate cache is encrypted, scoped to actual account UUID/VIN/local key and validity; missing secure storage becomes a controlled setup error with no certificate plaintext fallback. Account or VIN changes invalidate session bindings.

Final Smart Access verification runs 109 JVM tests with no failures/errors/skips and builds both debug APKs. Real JCE fake SAM covers authentication, ACKs, signed commands/status, tampering/replay/timeout and full minimum-MTU fragmentation; physical vehicle/HTTPS interoperability remains manual.

Recovered original 21f3bfc -> 21f3ebc adds a required phone/account relation step before certificates: POST /UserPhoneRelation/CheckUserPhoneRelation with real hex publicKey query and Platform/Language/PushNotificationToken list-valued JSON. Companion uses android/device language and the original empty nullable-push-token fallback, then still requires accepted full certificates.

Corrective follow-up to AF160 test count: after adding phone/account relation composition coverage, final suite runs 110 passing JVM tests and both debug APK builds; KB and diff checks pass. The earlier 109-test record is retained as history.

Corrective update to AF038/AF039: OLED Glass uses true #000000 backgrounds in all phone resource configurations, grayscale accents, translucent charcoal layered glass drawables and shared native typography; MainActivity always applies the dark theme and hides legacy system/light theme choices without deleting saved preferences.

OLED Glass dashboard uses a 28sp vehicle heading, section labels, horizontal e-Motor card, native monochrome door/trunk line icons with 64dp targets and named telemetry cards; existing card order, visibility, signed BLE status and command gating remain.
Watch app and Tile use grayscale accents on true-black backgrounds, rounded layered glass cards, grayscale native controls and 48dp watch action targets.
OLED Glass widget uses charcoal glass background and grayscale telemetry/map artwork; low tire pressure adds an explicit ! marker so warning does not depend on color.

Glass depth is implemented with gradient drawable layers and white edge highlights; no real background blur is used. Embedded map content and widget map snapshot are desaturated; hosted Togg ID login page styling is untouched.
OLED Glass home grid switches to one column below 380dp screen width or above 1.25 system font scale; tire cells share available row width, expose accessible labels and add ! to low pressure values.

Corrective update to AF108/AF109/AF112: manual dispatchToVehicleCloud is now cloud-only, returns plain API callback messages and never opens Trumore or navigation on error; explicit legacy deep-link helpers remain separate.

Main home screen provides Akıllı cihazıma aktar independently of ABRP setup and telemetry loading; shared map text and the ABRP card open the same OLED Glass VehicleRouteDialog. Actual sending requires a real non-demo vehicle and Togg ID session.

VehicleRouteDialog previews the resolved destination and ordered route roles, supports whole-route or single-target selection, invalidates resolved data after input edits, ignores stale asynchronous results and requires an explicit send tap.

Manual and background destination sends share one process-wide in-flight guard and callbacks complete once; a route POST retries only once after a non-permission HTTP401 token refresh, and ambiguous network/timeout failures never automatically resend.
